what: Let whoever launches a run, meaning one execution of a plan, tag it with short labels like `nightly` and filter run lists by them.
why: The user starts a dozen runs a day and cannot find this week's crozier runs without opening each. They want labels set once at launch and shown wherever runs are listed.
architecture: The engine, `onepipeline`, runs plans. It checks tags at launch and stores them in each run's record, which every run list reads, so it ships first.

units.name: Run ledger
units.summary: The ledger keeps each run's permanent record, which gains its tags.

reversible.title: Older runs
reversible.text: A record written before this change reads as a run with no tags.

reversible.title: Tags are fixed
reversible.text: Nothing changes a run's tags after launch, including resuming a stopped run, called adopting it.

decisions.name: Launch record
decisions.justification: older engines on other people's machines read launch records, and all would need updating.
decisions.summary: Each run's `launch.json`, written once at launch, gains a `tags` list.

units.name: Command line
units.summary: The command line starts and lists runs.

reversible.title: Bad tags are refused early
reversible.text: A malformed tag is refused, naming it, before anything is stored.

decisions.name: Tag format
decisions.justification: tightening it would invalidate tags stored on other people's machines.
decisions.summary: A tag is 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, starting with a letter; a run has at most eight.
decisions.artifact:
```text
tag   := [a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}
tags  := at most 8 distinct tags per run
```

decisions.name: `start --tag` and `runs --tag`
decisions.justification: other people's scripts will pass `--tag`; renaming it, or making `runs --tag` match any tag, silently breaks them.
decisions.summary: `start` takes one `--tag` per tag; `runs --tag` lists only runs carrying every tag named.
decisions.artifact:
```diff
 Usage: onepipeline start [OPTIONS] <PLAN>

 Options:
       --run-id <ID>        The run's id; generated when omitted
+      --tag <TAG>          Label the run; repeatable, at most 8. Fixed for the run's life
       --detach             Return once the driver is running
```

```diff
 Usage: onepipeline runs [OPTIONS]

 Options:
       --mine               Only runs this session launched
+      --tag <TAG>          Only runs carrying this tag; repeated, a run must carry every one
       --json               Print one JSON object per run
```

units.name: Read API
units.summary: The read API is the server behind the browser view.

reversible.title: Tags in the run list
reversible.text: `GET /runs` returns each run's `tags`, an empty list when it has none.

reversible.title: Tag filter
reversible.text: `GET /runs` takes a repeatable `tag` parameter, and a run must carry every tag given.

units.name: Browser view
units.summary: The browser view is the web page listing runs.

reversible.title: Tag chips
reversible.text: Each run in the list shows its tags.

reversible.title: Shareable filter
reversible.text: A tag filter above the list is kept in the page address, so a filtered list can be shared as a link.

units.name: Launch recipe
units.summary: The launch recipe is how this repository starts runs.

reversible.title: Pass-through
reversible.text: `just orchestrate --tag` hands each tag to `onepipeline start` unchanged.

acceptance_criteria: A run launched with `--tag crozier --tag nightly` shows both tags in every run list; filtering by both finds it.
A malformed tag is refused, creating no run.
Older runs show no tags, and adopted runs keep theirs.
`just orchestrate <plan> --tag nightly` launches a run tagged `nightly`.
